transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because I just keep snapping at people. It's gotten pretty bad lately. Like, we had this safety meeting recently, and I just... I started yelling before I could even stop myself. It just came out. And now the younger inspectors on the line, they act scared to even ask me anything. So, I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone.

When you're not having these outbursts, how is your overall mood most of the time? Would you say you feel normal and okay, or do you tend to feel irritable or down even when you're not snapping at people?

I haven't really thought about it, to be honest. I'm not really sure. I don't think I feel down or anything like that. I guess I just feel... regular, mostly? I just go in, do my inspections, and try to get through the day. It's really just those times when I snap that I notice something's wrong. Otherwise, I haven't really noticed feeling any particular way.
Have you always had a tendency to lose your temper or snap at people, or is this something that's relatively new for you?

No, it's definitely not something I've always done. I mean, I used to be pretty easygoing, actually. This... this snapping at people, it really started after that machinery accident we had at work. That was right after they changed our schedules to the overnight shift. It's been going on since then, so I guess that makes it about two years and four months now.

Since the accident and schedule change, have you noticed that you feel on edge or tense most of the time, even when nothing particular is happening? Or do you only feel that way right before or during situations that remind you of the accident?

I guess I'm pretty much always on edge now. It's not just when something reminds me of the accident. Even when I'm just sitting in the break room at work, or... or when I'm at choir rehearsal, I'm always watching the doors. I'm constantly listening for any sudden noises, like loud machinery, and I'm always checking to see who's walking up behind me. It's like my body just won't believe I'm actually safe anywhere.
Do you ever have unwanted memories or flashbacks of the accident that come back to you, even when you're not thinking about it? Or do you have nightmares about it?

Yes, I do. It doesn't even take much to trigger it. Just hearing a clank from a cart being pushed down the hall, or catching a whiff of hot oil... it can put me right back in that bay. It's like I'm seeing my coworker by the machine all over again, like it's happening right in front of me right at that moment. It's not a nightmare, it happens when I'm wide awake.
Have you been avoiding certain places at work, or avoiding doing certain tasks, because they might remind you of the accident or trigger those flashbacks?

Yes, I do. I mean, I go out of my way so I don't have to walk anywhere near the inspection bay at work. And I really won't talk about the accident if I can help it, I just change the subject. I even quit going to these industrial-history talks I used to really enjoy... just seeing the pictures of the old machinery sets me off now, so it's easier to just stay away from all of it.

Besides the industrial-history talks you mentioned, have you noticed that other things you used to enjoy doing—like hobbies, spending time with friends or family, or activities outside of work—just don't interest you anymore or don't bring you the pleasure they used to?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I still enjoy going to choir rehearsal every week, and I still like spending time with my family on the weekends. It's just the stuff related to work or machinery that I've stopped doing. Everything else is pretty much the same.
Have you noticed that you feel kind of emotionally numb or disconnected from people around you, even when you're doing things you normally enjoy like choir or spending time with family?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I still feel very close to my family, and I enjoy talking with the folks at choir just like I always have. I don't feel numb or cut off from them at all. It's really just the work stuff and the machinery that messes with me.

Since the accident, have you noticed that you think differently about yourself or the world? For example, do you find yourself thinking things like 'I can't trust anyone' or 'I'm not safe anywhere' or 'I'm a burden to others'?

Yes, I suppose I do think differently now. I definitely don't trust that plant or the people running it anymore. And as for myself... some days I just feel like I'm damaged goods. It's hard, because I feel like I can't even do the job I spent my whole life getting good at.

When you think about the accident or your job now, do you find yourself having a lot of negative thoughts—like blaming yourself for what happened, or thinking that people can't be trusted, or feeling like bad things are going to happen to you? How often do these kinds of thoughts come up?

Yes, I do. I mean, I think about it a lot, and I keep blaming myself. I keep thinking... if I had just pushed harder about the safety checks that day, or if I had stopped that run when it didn't feel right to me... maybe he wouldn't have gotten hurt so bad. It's hard not to think that it's my fault.
